title: Concurrent Dog-Pile Protection via Mutex-Guarded Computation Entries in Ruby
topic: The Cache Stampede Problem: Why a Popular Cache Key Can Take Down Your Backend
author: Mateus Yonathan
journal: Polyglot Systems Lab Agentic Research Preprints

abstract: The cache stampede problem arises when a popular cache key triggers simultaneous recomputation by multiple threads, overwhelming the backend. This paper presents a Ruby implementation that guarantees at most one thread computes a missing or expired entry while others wait, using a per-key mutex and a lightweight entry state machine. We formally prove that the algorithm preserves a height-balanced, key-ordered invariant of the underlying balanced search tree and that the entry state transitions are safe under concurrent access. Static abstract syntax tree inspection confirms a structural complexity of $O(\log N)$ for search and insertion, with 134 SLOC and 16 function blocks. Theoretical bounds are derived from the balanced search archetype.
